title: ork ai: print the agent guide and install the ork skill for Claude, Codex and Grok
lead: Add an "ai" command to ork, in the pattern of slicer's: "ork ai instructions" prints a short agent guide for driving ork from the command line, and "ork ai skill" prints or installs a SKILL.md built from the same text for Claude Code, Codex and Grok. The binary prints the text, so it cannot drift from the CLI. Neither subcommand needs the daemon.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Wave 4 (2026-11-02) was the first time an agent steered ork's own CLI through a wave, and the agent spent many calls learning what no help text says: which id each command takes (the ork- run id, not the run- slicer id), that answer and retry may not return until the role ends, that a role killed as hung needs a manual retry, that the status needs-you count can be stale, and which steps are the owner's alone (approve, adj answers, scope questions). The friction log is `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md` (F1-F22). The owner chose, 2026-11-02 (interactive question), an "ork ai" command over a checked-in skill file, and pass v1.2, so the text can follow the friction fixes that wave 4 files. slicer already has the pattern: "slicer ai instructions" and "slicer ai skill" with an output option and an install option that write .claude/skills/slicer/, .agents/skills/slicer/ and .grok/skills/slicer/ (checked 2026-11-02 with "slicer ai skill --help"; slicer S95 is the done slice). adj has "adj ai" (a paste-in AGENTS.md snippet). Nothing in slicer's roadmap covers ork's CLI (slicer find skill lists only slicer's own S95 and S106-S108). This slice is not a new capability that ork owns beyond its own CLI, so docs/boundaries.md needs no change.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/ai.go` (new): the "ai" command, its two subcommands, the install and output options and the JSON form.
- `internal/cli/ai_instructions.md` (new): the guide text, embedded with the standard library embed package. One source for both subcommands.
- `internal/cli/ai_test.go` (new): the tests below.
- `internal/cli/cli.go:225-262` (the command switch gets an "ai" case) and `internal/cli/cli.go:40` (the usage text gets an "ai" entry).
- `docs/guide.md:421` (section 14, Commands at a glance) and `docs/guide.md:204` (a short pointer in section 7, or the nearest fit).
- `README.md` (one line under the usage pointers, if the README lists commands; check with rg).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (entry under Unreleased, marked *proposed*).

This is an N-class slice: it touches no engine, daemon or cmd file. internal/cli output is UI, so it also gets a UI pass.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All in `internal/cli/ai_test.go`, using the run helper from `internal/cli/cli_test.go:125` with an App that has no daemon socket and no Start function.

- TestAIInstructionsPrintsGuideWithoutDaemon: "ai instructions" exits 0, prints text that starts with a heading line and names the ork- id rule, and never dials the daemon. Fails first because "ai" is an unknown command (exit 2 with a usage line).
- TestAISkillPrintsSkillMD: "ai skill" exits 0 and prints text that starts with YAML front matter holding name: ork and a one-line description, followed by the same body as the guide.
- TestAISkillOutputWritesOneFile: with the output option and a path in a temp directory, the file holds the printed text, parent directories are created, and stdout lists the path.
- TestAISkillInstallWritesThreeDirs: with the install option in a temp working directory, the files .claude/skills/ork/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/ork/SKILL.md and .grok/skills/ork/SKILL.md exist with identical text, and stdout lists the three paths.
- TestAISkillInstallRefusesDifferentText: a destination that holds different text is not replaced and the command exits 1 naming the path; with the force option it is replaced; identical text is left alone and exits 0.
- TestAIJSON: with --json, "ai instructions" prints {"text": ...} and "ai skill --output PATH" prints {"written": [PATH]} (*proposed* shape, matching slicer's machine-readable option).
- TestAIUnknownSubcommandIsUsageError: "ai", "ai bogus" and "ai instructions extra" exit 2 with a usage line that lists the two subcommands.
- TestAIGuideCommandsAreInUsage: every line of the guide that starts with "ork " (after trimming a leading dash or indent) names a command word and every option that appears in the usage text (`internal/cli/cli.go:40`); a guide line that names a command or option the CLI does not have fails. This keeps the text from drifting.
- TestAIGuideNamesOwnerOnlySteps: the guide states that approve, adj answers and scope or design questions are the owner's, and says an agent relays the owner's pick from an interactive question only.
- TestUsageListsAI: the usage text lists the "ai" command, and the existing line-length test (`internal/cli/run_test.go:553`) still passes.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first, in the order above. Confirm each fails for the stated reason before writing code.
2. Write `internal/cli/ai_instructions.md` after reading the current help (go run ./cmd/ork --help), `docs/guide.md` sections 7-12, and `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`. Every claim about behavior must be checked against the code or a command run in the worktree; do not copy a claim from the friction log without checking it. Keep it under about 80 lines, short plain sentences, ASCII. Cover, in order:
   - What ork is for an agent (one sentence) and that every command takes --json.
   - Check: ork doctor and ork status; the daemon starts on demand and a restart is the owner's step after a new build.
   - Launch: ork run and ork wave start with the confirmation flags; the plan is shown first.
   - Ids: which id each command takes (verify for approve, check, fix, stop, answer, retry, dismiss, file).
   - Steer: ork answer, ork fix, ork retry after a role is killed as hung, ork stop; what a hung kill means and that sleeping counts as time.
   - Owner-only steps: approve, check, adj answers, scope and design questions. Ask the owner in an interactive question, then relay the pick.
   - Watching: how to wait without a tight poll; a state change shows in the status run lines.
   - Do not paste any slicer relay contract text (project rule); refer to "slicer ai relay".
   Add the front matter for the skill in `ai.go`, not in the .md file, so the guide stays plain text.
3. Write `internal/cli/ai.go`: parse the subcommand with the same flag style as `internal/cli/vendor.go:20-40`; the install option writes the three directories under the working directory (*proposed*: the current directory, as the owner has not named another root; add a directory option only if a test needs it); the force option as in the failing test. Use only the standard library.
4. Add the switch case and the usage lines (keep them within the width the existing test allows).
5. Docs: the Commands at a glance table and a short pointer. Mark the command *proposed* until an adj record decides it.
6. Do NOT touch `internal/daemon`, `internal/engine`, `cmd`, or any slicer file; do not run the install option on this repository (that would create .claude/skills here; the owner decides later whether to check one in).
7. CHANGELOG entry last, under Unreleased, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.
8. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- Run "ork ai instructions" and "ork ai skill" from a source build in the worktree and read both outputs; run "ork ai skill --output" into `.scratch/` only.
- Confirm by hand that every command line in the guide runs or is accepted by "ork help" text.
- [HUMAN CHECK] After landing and a rebuild, the owner reads "ork ai instructions" once and says whether it matches how an agent should drive ork, and decides whether to install the skill in a project.
